leftColumn.title: Futures & Forwards
leftColumn.subtitle: symmetric commitment contract
bullets: Holder is committed (obligated) to buy or sell at maturity
Costs nothing upfront to enter (except margin deposits)
Symmetric payoff with unlimited upside and downside risk

rightColumn.title: Options Contracts
rightColumn.subtitle: asymmetric choice contract
bullets: Holder has the right, but zero obligation, to buy or sell
Buyer pays an upfront option premium to the seller (writer)
Asymmetric payoff: buyer downside is capped at premium paid

beats.en_narration: A futures contract is an obligation for both buyer and seller entered with zero upfront cost. An option contract grants the buyer a right without obligation, purchased with an upfront premium.

subtitlePhrases.text: Futures obligate both sides at zero upfront fee;
options grant rights for a premium.

beats.en_subtitle: Calls buy, puts sell; European exercises at maturity, American exercises anytime.

leftColumn.title: 4 Positions & Calls vs Puts
leftColumn.subtitle: 1 CBOE contract = 100 shares
bullets: Long Call: buyer right to buy | Short Call: writer obligation to sell
Long Put: buyer right to sell | Short Put: writer obligation to buy
Strike Price (K) is fixed exercise price; Maturity (T) is final expiry

rightColumn.title: European vs American Style
rightColumn.subtitle: when can the holder exercise?
bullets: European Option: can be exercised ONLY on the maturity date itself
American Option: can be exercised at ANY time up to expiration
Most exchange-traded single-stock options (like CBOE Google) are American

beats.en_narration: A call option gives the right to buy; a put option gives the right to sell. European options can only be exercised at maturity, whereas American options can be exercised at any time up to expiration.

beats.en_subtitle: Higher strike lowers call value and raises put value; longer maturity raises both.

leftColumn.title: Call Price Dynamics
leftColumn.subtitle: CBOE Google Spot: $532.20 / $532.34
bullets: Call option prices DECREASE as the strike price (K) increases
Higher strike means a higher hurdle before the right to buy pays off
Call prices INCREASE as time to maturity (T) increases

rightColumn.title: Put Price Dynamics
rightColumn.subtitle: CBOE Google Spot: $532.20 / $532.34
bullets: Put option prices INCREASE as the strike price (K) increases
Higher strike locks in a higher selling price for the underlying stock
Put prices also INCREASE as time to maturity (T) increases

beats.en_narration: For call options, a higher strike price decreases value, while for put options, a higher strike increases value. For both types, longer expiration periods provide more time value and increase the premium.

subtitlePhrases.text: Higher strike lowers call value and raises put value;
